clue.text: Spooner's city sends for fortune tellers

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words found here trade their starts

parts.note: Bristol is a city in south-west England
to send for someone is to call them

explanation.surface: A city dispatches someone to fetch its fortune tellers.
explanation.walkthrough: BRISTOL CALLS with the opening sounds swapped gives CRISTAL BALLS, said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass globes are the props clairvoyants gaze into, so the objects stand for the soothsayers by metonymy.

clue.text: Utter tosh about US estate agent

parts.note: utter, as in an utter fool, means real or complete

indicators.note: about signals the word for tosh being turned round

parts.note: tosh is nonsense, rot

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an American property seller's patter as complete rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Realtor is the standard American term for a property broker who sells houses.

clue.text: Jam makers entering S&M clubs, perhaps in costume

indicators.note: entering means the jam makers go inside the two letters

parts.note: the letters S and M taken as written
the WI, Britain's Women's Institute, is famous for making jam
clubs is one example of a suit of playing cards

explanation.surface: Jam-making ladies turn up at kinky clubs in fancy dress.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI (Women's Institute) is a British women's organisation known for jam and cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathing costume is the British phrase for an outfit worn for swimming.

clue.text: Spots top pilot circling capital of Nepal

indicators.note: circling means the pilot word goes round the letter from Nepal

parts.note: an ace is a fighter pilot with many kills, a top flyer

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An airman notices something while flying a loop around Kathmandu.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is the skin condition marked by pimples, which are colloquially called spots.

clue.text: Zany Polish butcher in Soho

parts.note: to buff is to polish

indicators.note: to butcher is to mangle, so the following letters are mangled

explanation.surface: A crazy Polish meat seller trading in London's Soho district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a nationality but is the verb; 'butcher' rearranges IN SOHO into OONISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Clownish, foolish and comic behaviour is what a zany person shows, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Catalogues Blair's stash regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: An inventory of a former prime minister's secret hoard.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalogue and an inventory register are both ordered records of items, so the plurals match.

clue.text: Singular old ladies describing student couplings

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: describing, in the sense of drawing a line around, puts one piece round another

parts.note: a man's old lady is slang for his wife
L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Unmarried elderly women recount how students pair off.
explanation.definitionFit: A swivel is a rotating joint linking two parts, a kind of mechanical connector.

clue.text: Burning Tory Union Jack quota?

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party
the Union Jack is the flag of the United Kingdom
a ration is an allotted quota

explanation.surface: A Conservative's allowance of British flags to set alight at a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A conflagration is a great fire, so it is a large-scale act of combustion.

clue.text: Small gangs of little people on speed, oddly unruffled

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small
an elf is one of the little people of folklore
posses are bands or gangs of people

indicators.note: oddly means taking the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Little gangs of fairy folk high on amphetamine, strangely calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Composed and calm describe someone not flustered, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Pub shunning novelty? Cheers!

indicators.note: shunning means the pub word is left out

parts.note: an innovation is something new, a novelty
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A traditional tavern rejecting new things raises a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A round of applause and acclaim is what loud cheering amounts to.

clue.text: Joyful female, not initially impatient

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: restive means restless or impatient

explanation.surface: A woman who was happy, though not at first restless.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebratory and merry are near synonyms, as in a festive mood at a party.

clue.text: Lots of tubby Estonians on vacation

parts.note: tubby means fat

indicators.note: a word on vacation is emptied of its insides, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: Plenty of overweight people from Estonia away on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot in life is one's destiny, so lots and fates are synonyms.

clue.text: X-rated Barking fleshpot

indicators.note: barking, as in barking mad, means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A sleazy den of vice in Barking, an east London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is also a district of east London, which makes the surface read as a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult magazines were kept out of children's reach on the highest rack, so the phrase means pornographic.

clue.text: Use those to pay for treatment

indicators.note: use here means put the letters to use in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Instructions to spend some money on medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteopathy is a therapy manipulating bones and muscles, one form of medical care.

clue.text: Show Peace Nobelist ignoring royal greeting

parts.note: to air something is to show it publicly

indicators.note: ignoring means the royal letters are omitted

parts.note: Henry Kissinger won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1973
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher

explanation.surface: A peace prize winner snubbing a royal welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss blown near the cheek without contact is a social salutation.

clue.text: Posh slob stripped in northern city

indicators.note: stripped means each word loses its outer letters, keeping only its middle

explanation.surface: A rich slacker undressed somewhere in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital of Norway, a city in northern Europe.

clue.text: Resolute nana belted bumpkin, Cockneys say

indicators.note: Cockneys say signals the words are heard in a London East End accent

parts.note: nana is a gran, belted is hit, a bumpkin is a hick, and a Cockney speaker leaves off the aitch of the last two

explanation.surface: A tough granny thumped a country yokel, East Enders report.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop their H's: GRAN 'IT 'ICK, said aloud, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Granitic literally means like granite, figuratively unyielding and steadfast.

clue.text: Gripped wound, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: wound, as in wound a bandage around, means wrapped

explanation.surface: An injury, so people say, that someone was clutching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like an injury; it is the past tense of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held spellbound by a story means one is enthralled and totally absorbed.

clue.text: Saw tramp in empty pub

indicators.note: in means the tramp goes inside the emptied pub
an empty word has its insides removed, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: a rover is a wanderer or tramp

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a vagrant inside a deserted bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see; it is a noun, an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old maxim or saying, a synonym for an adage.

clue.text: Administering cure soon is critical

indicators.note: administering means dealing out or managing, so the letters are dealt into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor's urgent advice: giving treatment quickly is vital.
explanation.definitionFit: Censorious means severely fault-finding, a synonym for judgmental or critical.

clue.text: Havoc to be repeated over month

indicators.note: over means the answer spans over the run of words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Chaos is going to happen again for a whole month.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth month of the year in the calendar.

clue.text: Novelist Tom Wolfe's last letter

parts.note: tom is slang for a prostitute, as is trollop

indicators.note: last letter means only the final letter of the writer's surname is used

explanation.surface: The American writer Tom Wolfe's final piece of correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom Wolfe' reads as the American author, but Tom is a separate slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope was a Victorian author of the Barsetshire books.

clue.text: Starts to loot your store of lavatory disinfectant

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Instructions to raid your supply of toilet cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Lysol is a brand of household germ-killing cleaner.

clue.text: Pays attention to revolutionary attack

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the phrase is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to set on someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: Someone takes heed of a rebel assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to observe or heed it, so the verb forms agree.

clue.text: Extremely flavoursome tapioca and cheese

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extreme, outermost letters of each word

explanation.surface: A very tasty tapioca pudding served with cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white brined Greek variety made from sheep's milk.

clue.text: Love poetry beginning to trigger disquiet

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
verse is poetry

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Romantic verse starts to cause unease.
explanation.definitionFit: Overset is an old verb for upset or disturb, so it means to unsettle someone.

clue.text: Unlimited real food, fit for consumption

indicators.note: unlimited means the word loses its limits, its first and last letters

parts.note: table can mean the food served, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: An endless supply of genuine food that is safe to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible things can safely be eaten, the same as being suitable to swallow.

clue.text: Excitedly recalls bendy female performers

indicators.note: excitedly means in an agitated way, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly remembers a supple person.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancers who perform a Middle Eastern style of stomach dance are usually women.
